newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner-Moody's downgrade won't affect financing.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner-Moody's downgrade won't affect financing.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG said on Wednesday that a decision by Moody's Investors Service to downgrade the bank's long-term deposit and financial strength ratings would not affect financing volumes or costs.
Dresdner said in a statement that, "The bank expects neither financing costs nor volumes to be impaired."
Moody's had earlier downgraded Dresdner's long-term debt, counterparty and deposit ratings to Aa1 from AAA, subordinated debt to Aa2 from Aa1 and the bank's financial strength rating to B+ from A.
Moody's said that despite the cuts it viewed Dresdner as one of Europe's strongest and better managed financial institutions and that this opinion remains reflected in the bank's credit ratings.
Dresdner said such remarks showed that the rating service continued to highly regard the bank.
